answer: Treat identity like a garden: anything planted in bulk without tending dies. A sybil farm can scatter a thousand seeds in an instant, but each must be watered with scarce judgment to survive. Make reputation ferrous - heavy, slow to forge, bearing weight only after real heat and pressure. Bind every account to a history of witnessed work, and let influence climb from the nadir upward, one verifiable season at a time. Fake crowds then cost more to maintain than to create, and the ledger follows the gardener, not the swarm.
